L117.assumptions: L117-I01: Choose factor, response and matched conditions; feedback identifies the remaining untestable element.
L117.limits: Depth: Support does not establish a unique explanation; growth also involves respiration and allocation. A useful hypothesis is revisable and must not redefine every possible result as success. A hypothesis is not a wish. Agreement does not permanently prove it, and unmeasured “health” is not a synonym for height.

L118.assumptions: L118-I01: Repair water, independent units, randomisation and blocking; feedback identifies remaining weaknesses. Compare one plant × twelve readings with four plants × three readings.
L118.limits: Depth: The experimental unit independently receives treatment; biological sources and treatment units can differ. Pairing before/after values measures within-plant change, but the two values are not independent samples. Repeated readings do not increase independent biological sample size; random allocation and matched conditions address different problems.

L119.assumptions: L119-I01: Repair axes, toggle original/unverified-28 cm records and choose investigation versus unjustified deletion. Compare mean changes.
L119.limits: Depth: Range depends on sample size and does not directly measure accuracy. Accuracy concerns closeness to a reference; precision concerns agreement among repeated readings. No significance tests or confidence intervals are calculated here. Range=max−min, not mean±range, instrument error or a CI. An unusual observation requires evidence about its cause.

L120.assumptions: L120-I01: Select faulty or repaired design, then universal, descriptive or conditional conclusion; feedback checks whether the claim overreaches.
L120.limits: Depth: Allocation helps internal causal interpretation; broader sampling helps external applicability. Neither replaces the other. Statistical uncertainty, mechanism measurements and design bias are also distinct questions. Limitations do not mean no evidence; random allocation does not represent every plant; a plausible mechanism is not a measured mechanism.
